key_insight: The paper shows that accurate phase-stability assessment of inorganic perovskite halides requires correcting for true sample temperature during in-situ thermal treatment, using CsPbCl3 as a reference to validate the method.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more reliable thermal-testing workflow for screening perovskite and double-perovskite absorber stability under operating-like heating conditions.
method: Use CsPbCl3 as a baseline material to calibrate and verify thermal behavior.
Compare phase evolution with in-situ temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction.
Refine temperature estimates with a control substrate to better match actual sample temperature.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that stoichiometry, crystal structure, and particle morphology were analyzed, and in-situ XRD was used to identify phase transitions and decomposition temperatures for CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on accurate thermal calibration and reproducible in-situ measurement conditions, so misestimated sample temperature could lead to incorrect stability conclusions.
paper_title: Thermal Corrections and Analysis on the Phase Stability of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 during In-Situ Thermal Treatment
